**My reasoning, as this farmer:**

I am 72 years old. My back hurts in the mornings. My son works in the city — he sends money home but is not here to help in the fields. I have 8 mu of flat land, same land I've farmed for fifty years. I know this land. I do not need to experiment.

I will grow winter wheat and summer maize, just as I always do. The government promotes this rotation, it feeds my family, and I can sell the surplus to the grain depot. I know the prices. I know the timing.

For wheat — I already planted it last October. Right now it is April. I put down the base fertilizer then, and I will topdress urea at jointing stage, same as every year. I irrigate four times: winter water in November to protect the roots from freezing, jointing water in March, heading water in late April, and a grain-filling irrigation if the weather is dry. My neighbor says three times is enough, but I am afraid of losing yield. I spray twice — once for aphids and powdery mildew in spring, once for weevils before harvest.

After wheat harvest in June, I call the machinery station to direct-seed maize into the stubble. No-tillage saves my body and costs less. I throw down the compound fertilizer at planting and topdress urea when it reaches knee height. Summer rain usually takes care of most of the water, but I irrigate once at silking if August is dry, because I cannot afford a bad year.

I use improved wheat seed from the county seed station — Shiluan variety. For maize I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid, which the village cooperative sells. I have used it for years. I trust it.
